primary.poolable_reason: THE ONE TOPIC THE TRIAGE CALLED POOL POSSIBLE, AND READING IT CLOSES IT TOO. Both trials do register a stroke endpoint and dabigatran is the intervention in both, which is why the outcome screen passed them. But NCT00262600 (RE-LY) enrols ATRIAL FIBRILLATION and compares dabigatran against WARFARIN, while NCT02239120 (RE-SPECT ESUS) enrols EMBOLIC STROKE OF UNDETERMINED SOURCE -- a different population, defined by the absence of a known cardiac source -- and compares dabigatran against ASPIRIN. Different disease, different comparator. Averaging an anticoagulant-versus-warfarin contrast in AF with an anticoagulant-versus-aspirin contrast in ESUS is not a pool of one question.

primary.what_this_verdict_does_not_establish: NOT that any of these trials is poor -- each is registered, randomised where it says so, and reports its primary. NOT that the drug is ineffective. NOT that no poolable question exists in this area: only that the question this page's title asks cannot be answered by pooling the trials this page carries. If a further eligible trial is identified, this verdict should be revisited.
